top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) is the only writer on the slate. On the common criteria, public knowledge of Blinding (the Orbitor sequence) and Solenoid points to a distinctive voice, large patterned structures that look built rather than merely long, and a sustained imaginative project that treats memory, the body and dream as one metaphysical enterprise. The citation should rest on the prose, with poetry named only as a root, since the poetry-as-base claim is a hypothesis I cannot verify. The main risk remains whether the late novels deepen their image systems or recirculate them, and whether the density and musicality of the Romanian prose survive translation. These are limits of access, not findings against the work. They do not justify no award, so P000 is ranked last. This rests on general public knowledge and colleagues' stated views, not on independent verification or on my having read the works, and the unanimous opening ranking is not treated as merit.
